summary: To do the mitzvah of Shema you must have in mind to do it. This mishnah also teaches when you may stop in the middle of Shema to greet someone.
stIntro: The first question discussed in the mishna is the question of intent.

chunks.en: If someone was reading the Torah
chunks.st: One who was reading the sections of the Torah which comprise Shema,

chunks.en: and the time came to say Shema,
chunks.st: and the time for the recitation of the morning or evening Shema arrived,

chunks.en: if he had in mind to do the mitzvah,
chunks.st: if he focused his heart,

chunks.en: he did the mitzvah. And if not,
chunks.st: he fulfilled his obligation
chunks.basisNote: Steinsaltz's text stops at 'he did the mitzvah'; 'and if not' follows Bartenura.

chunks.en: he did not do the mitzvah.
chunks.st: and need not repeat Shema in order to fulfill his obligation.
chunks.stMore: This is true even if he failed to recite the requisite blessings (Rabbeinu Ḥananel). Ab initio, one may not interrupt the recitation of Shema. The tanna’im, however, disagree over how strict one must be in this regard. They distinguish between interruptions between paragraphs and interruptions within each paragraph.
chunks.basisNote: Steinsaltz's text does not have these words; following Bartenura.

chunks.en: Between the sections, he may greet someone out of respect, and answer,
chunks.st: At the breaks between paragraphs, one may greet an individual due to the respect that he is obligated to show him, and one may respond to another’s greeting due to respect.

chunks.en: and in the middle, he may greet someone he fears, and answer.
chunks.st: And in the middle of each paragraph one may greet an individual due to the fear that the individual may harm him if he fails do so (Me’iri) and one may respond to another’s greeting due to fear.

words.note: Someone he is afraid of, like a king or a dangerous person.

chunks.en: These are the words of Rabbi Meir.
chunks.st: This is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:
chunks.stMore: There is a distinction between greeting someone and responding to his greeting.

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: in the middle he may greet someone he fears,
chunks.st: In the middle of each paragraph, one may greet another due to fear

chunks.en: and answer someone he respects;
chunks.st: and respond due to respect.

chunks.en: between the sections he may greet someone he respects,
chunks.st: In the breaks between paragraphs, one may greet another due to respect

chunks.en: and answer "Shalom" to anyone.
chunks.st: and respond with a greeting to any person who greets him, whether or not he is obligated to show him respect.

summary: This mishnah lists the places "between the sections" of Shema and its brachos, and explains why the parts of Shema are in their order.
stIntro: As for what constitutes a paragraph,

chunks.en: These are the places "between the sections":
chunks.st: these are the breaks between the paragraphs:

chunks.en: between the first bracha and the second,
chunks.st: Between the first blessing and the second,

chunks.en: between the second and Shema,
chunks.st: between the second and Shema,

chunks.en: and between Shema and "Vehayah im shamoa,"
chunks.st: between Shema and the second paragraph: If you indeed heed My commandments [VeHaya im Shamoa],

words.note: The second paragraph of Shema.

chunks.en: between "Vehayah im shamoa" and "Vayomer,"
chunks.st: between VeHaya im Shamoa and the third paragraph: And the Lord spoke [VaYomer]

words.note: The third paragraph of Shema, about tzitzis.

chunks.en: between "Vayomer" and "Emes Veyatziv."
chunks.st: and between VaYomer and True and Firm [emet veyatziv], the blessing that follows Shema.
chunks.stMore: The Rabbis held that each blessing and each paragraph of Shema constitutes its own entity, and treat interruptions between them as between the paragraphs.

words.note: The bracha right after Shema in the morning.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda, however, says:

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.he: בֵּין וַיֹּאמֶר לֶאֱמֶת וְיַצִּיב לֹא יַפְסִיק.
chunks.en: between "Vayomer" and "Emes Veyatziv" one may not stop.
chunks.st: Between VaYomer and emet veyatziv, which begins the blessing that follows Shema, one may not interrupt at all.
chunks.stMore: According to Rabbi Yehuda, these must be recited consecutively. Since the paragraphs of Shema are not adjacent to one another in the Torah, and they are not recited in the order in which they appear, the mishna explains their placement.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korchah said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korḥa said:

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.he: לָמָּה קָדְמָה שְׁמַע לִוְהָיָה אִם שָׁמֹעַ,
chunks.en: Why does Shema come before "Vehayah im shamoa"?
chunks.st: Why, in the mitzva of the recitation of Shema, did the portion of Shema precede that of VeHaya im Shamoa?

chunks.en: So that a person will accept
chunks.st: This is so that one will first accept upon himself

chunks.en: Hashem as his King first,
chunks.st: the yoke of the kingdom of Heaven, the awareness of God and God’s unity,

words.note: Accepting Hashem as our King.

chunks.he: וְאַחַר כָּךְ יְקַבֵּל עָלָיו עֹל מִצְוֹת.
chunks.en: and after that he accepts the mitzvos.
chunks.st: and only then accept upon himself the yoke of the mitzvot, which appears in the paragraph of VeHaya im Shamoa.

chunks.en: And "Vehayah im shamoa" comes before "Vayomer,"
chunks.st: Why did VeHaya im Shamoa precede VaYomer?

chunks.he: שֶׁוְהָיָה אִם שָׁמֹעַ נוֹהֵג בַּיּוֹם וּבַלַּיְלָה,
chunks.en: because "Vehayah im shamoa" applies day and night,
chunks.st: Because the paragraph of VeHaya im Shamoa is practiced both by day and by night,

chunks.en: but "Vayomer" only applies in the daytime.
chunks.st: while VaYomer, which discusses the mitzva of ritual fringes, is only practiced during the day.

words.note: Because it is about tzitzis, which we wear in the daytime.

summary: This mishnah teaches what happens if you say Shema too quietly, unclearly, out of order, or with a mistake.

chunks.he: הַקּוֹרֵא אֶת שְׁמַע וְלֹא הִשְׁמִיעַ לְאָזְנוֹ,
chunks.en: If someone says Shema so quietly that his own ears cannot hear it,
chunks.st: One who recites Shema and did not recite in a manner audible to his own ear,
chunks.stMore: either because he read inaudibly or because he is deaf,

chunks.en: he did the mitzvah. Rabbi Yosi says,
chunks.st: fulfilled his obligation. Rabbi Yosei says:

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: he did not do the mitzvah.
chunks.st: He did not fulfill his obligation.

chunks.en: If he read without saying each letter carefully,
chunks.st: One who recited Shema and was not sufficiently precise in his enunciation of its letters,

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosi says he did the mitzvah,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says: He fulfilled his obligation.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says he did not.
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says: He did not fulfill his obligation.

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: If someone reads it out of order,
chunks.st: One who recited Shema out of order, meaning he did not read the verses sequentially,

chunks.en: he did not do the mitzvah.
chunks.st: he did not fulfill his obligation.

chunks.en: If he read and made a mistake,
chunks.st: One who recited and erred,

chunks.en: he goes back to the place of the mistake.
chunks.st: should return to the place in Shema that he erred.

summary: Workers may say Shema while up in a tree or on a wall, but they must come down to daven Shemoneh Esrei.
stIntro: The primary issue in this mishna is the requisite degree of concentration when reciting Shema.

chunks.en: Workers may say Shema at the top of a tree
chunks.st: Laborers engaged in their work may recite Shema while standing atop the tree

chunks.en: or at the top of a row of stones in a wall,
chunks.st: or atop the course of stones in a wall under construction,

words.note: A row of stones in a wall that is being built.

chunks.he: מַה שֶּׁאֵינָן רַשָּׁאִין לַעֲשׂוֹת כֵּן בַּתְּפִלָּה:
chunks.en: which they may not do for davening Shemoneh Esrei.
chunks.st: which they are not permitted to do for the Amida prayer, which requires intent of the heart.

words.note: Here "tefillah" means Shemoneh Esrei.

summary: A chassan does not have to say Shema on his wedding night, because he is too busy thinking. But Rabban Gamliel said it anyway, because he did not want to stop accepting Hashem as King even for a moment.

chunks.en: A chassan does not have to say Shema at night
chunks.st: A groom is exempt from the recitation of Shema on

words.note: A chassan is a groom who just got married.

chunks.en: on the first night after his wedding, until after Shabbos,
chunks.st: the first night of his marriage, which was generally Wednesday night, until Saturday night,

chunks.en: if he has not yet done the act of marriage.
chunks.st: if he has not taken action and consummated the marriage,
chunks.stMore: as he is preoccupied by concerns related to consummation of the marriage. The mishna relates that

chunks.en: There was a story with Rabban Gamliel, who said Shema
chunks.st: there was an incident where Rabban Gamliel married a woman and recited Shema

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah, head of the Sanhedrin.

chunks.en: on the first night after he got married.
chunks.st: even the first night.

chunks.en: His students said to him,
chunks.st: His students said to him:

chunks.en: "Didn't you teach us,
chunks.st: Didn’t our teacher teach us

chunks.he: רַבֵּנוּ, שֶׁחָתָן פָּטוּר מִקְּרִיאַת שְׁמַע בַּלַּיְלָה הָרִאשׁוֹן.
chunks.en: our Rebbi, that a chassan does not have to say Shema on the first night?"
chunks.st: that a groom is exempt from the recitation of Shema?

chunks.en: He said to them,
chunks.st: He answered them:

chunks.en: "I will not listen to you and take off from myself
chunks.st: Nevertheless, I am not listening to you to refrain from reciting Shema, and in so doing preclude myself from the acceptance of

chunks.en: Hashem as my King, even for one moment."
chunks.st: the yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven, for even one moment.

words.note: Accepting Hashem as our King.

summary: Rabban Gamliel washed himself on the first night after his wife died, even though a mourner may not wash. He explained that he was a very delicate person who would suffer without washing.
stIntro: The mishna relates another episode portraying unusual conduct by Rabban Gamliel.

chunks.en: He washed on the first night after his wife died.
chunks.st: He bathed on the first night after his wife died.

chunks.en: His students said to him,
chunks.st: His students said to him:

chunks.en: "Didn't you teach us,
chunks.st: Have you not taught us,

chunks.en: our Rebbi, that a mourner may not wash?"
chunks.st: our teacher, that a mourner is prohibited to bathe?

words.note: An avel is someone whose close relative just died.

chunks.en: He said to them,
chunks.st: He answered them:

chunks.en: "I am not like all other people,
chunks.st: I am not like other people,

chunks.en: I am very delicate."
chunks.st: I am delicate [istenis].
chunks.stMore: For me, not bathing causes actual physical distress, and even a mourner need not suffer physical distress as part of his mourning.
chunks.basisNote: Steinsaltz: delicate. Bartenura: he caught cold easily and would suffer.

words.note: Someone so sensitive that not washing would make him sick.

summary: When Rabban Gamliel's servant Tavi died, he accepted comforting like for a family member. He explained that Tavi was a very special, righteous servant.

chunks.en: And when Tavi, his servant, died,
chunks.st: And when his slave, Tavi, died,

chunks.en: he let people come comfort him.
chunks.st: Rabban Gamliel accepted condolences for his death as one would for a close family member.

words.note: Words of comfort said to a mourner.

chunks.en: His students said to him,
chunks.st: His students said to him:

chunks.en: "Didn't you teach us, our Rebbi,
chunks.st: Have you not taught us, our teacher,

chunks.en: that we do not accept comforting for servants?"
chunks.st: that one does not accept condolences for the death of slaves?

chunks.en: He said to them,
chunks.st: Rabban Gamliel said to his students:

chunks.he: אֵין טָבִי עַבְדִּי כִּשְׁאָר כָּל הָעֲבָדִים,
chunks.en: "My servant Tavi is not like all other servants;
chunks.st: My slave, Tavi, is not like all the rest of the slaves,

chunks.en: he was a good, honest man."
chunks.st: he was virtuous
chunks.stMore: and it is appropriate to accord him the same respect accorded to a family member.

summary: A chassan may say Shema on his first night if he wants. Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says not everyone should act as if he is so holy that he can concentrate.
stIntro: With regard to the recitation of Shema on one’s wedding night, the Sages said that

chunks.en: A chassan, if he wants to say
chunks.st: if, despite his exemption, a groom wishes to recite

words.note: A groom who just got married.

chunks.en: Shema on the first night,
chunks.st: Shema on the first night,

chunks.he: קוֹרֵא. רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר,
chunks.en: may say it. Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says,
chunks.st: he may do so. Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah, head of the Sanhedrin.

chunks.en: Not everyone who wants to take
chunks.st: Not everyone who wishes to assume

chunks.en: the name of being very holy may take it.
chunks.explain: Acting extra holy when people don't see you that way is showing off.
chunks.st: the reputation of a God-fearing person may assume it,
chunks.stMore: and consequently, not everyone who wishes to recite Shema on his wedding night may do so.

words.note: A name for being a very holy, God-fearing person.
